subject: Mutual Action Plan & security acceptance sprint — Finly evaluation
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Arielle Martin <arielle@finly.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-26 09:12 -0700
Subject: Mutual Action Plan & security acceptance sprint — Finly evaluation

Arielle — thanks for the kickoff this morning. Per our conversation, I’m drafting a compact MAP focused solely on the security/compliance gates you flagged so we can get to a fast acceptance decision. High level asks below; I attached a working checklist (Finly-MAP-security-checklist.xlsx) that we can iterate in-drive.

Goal: finish evidence handoff and legal redlines so Finly can make an acceptance decision during the week of July 31.

Security gates scoped for this MAP:
- SOC 2 Type II: provide the latest report + control narrative excerpts relevant to data separation, incident response, and change management.
- SIG / CAIQ: deliver a completed SIG mapping (we’ll highlight any compensating controls where the template differs).
- DPA: legal redlines (Finly to propose, Redwood to respond). Key items to resolve: data retention windows, EU residency, deletion API SLA, subprocessor list and KMS/keys.
- Data retention details: we propose "session-level logs (90 days) / backups (180 days) / snapshots (30 days)" as a starting point — open to adjustments by region (EU customers may require 90/90/30).

Proposed owners & milestones (short sprint):
- Jul 27 EOD: Redwood to upload SOC2 extract and control excerpts (owner: Jordan)
- Jul 28 EOD: SIG answers (owner: Kimberly)
- Jul 29 EOD: Redwood legal initial response to DPA redline (owner: Ben)
- Jul 30: Evidence review meeting (30m) with Finly security + legal
- Jul 31: Final review / acceptance decision

Open questions from our side:
1) Do you require EU-residency for all production data or only for EU tenant records?
2) Can you share a short example of the retention policy language you expect in the DPA?
3) Any specific CAIQ controls you want prioritized for the SIG mapping?

I’ll add these into the checklist and keep the drive link up to date. If this timeline is too aggressive, tell me which milestone you want to push and we’ll adapt.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: Finly-MAP-security-checklist.xlsx
From: Arielle Martin <arielle@finly.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.g@finly.com>
Date: 2028-07-26 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & security acceptance sprint — Finly evaluation

Jordan — appreciate the concise plan and timeline. Quick answers and a couple of asks:

- EU residency: we need all production customer data (including backups) for EU-based customers to be stored in EU regions. For mixed accounts, only the EU subset must be resident.
- Retention language: we prefer explicit buckets in the DPA (logs/7d, session traces/90d, backups/180d, account archives/7 years for regulated customers). Can you confirm Redwood can support that split?
- Deletion API: critical — we need a documented API endpoint and expected max completion SLA (e.g., 72 hours) for deletion requests impacting EU data.

We reviewed the SOC2 ask and will expect the usual redaction for customer-identifiable info; SAMIR and I will validate once you post the extract. I’ll also attach our DPA redline to the thread (we’ll upload to the Drive).

If the Redwood team can meet the milestones above, we can target our acceptance call on Jul 31.

Thanks — Arielle
Arielle Martin
Head of Security & Compliance
Finly
arielle@finly.com | +1 646-555-0123

Attachments: Finly-DPA-redline-v1.docx (to follow in Drive)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Arielle Martin <arielle@finly.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-27 08:54 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & security acceptance sprint — Finly evaluation

Thanks Arielle — confirming next steps against your points and owners:

- EU residency: Redwood supports region-scoped tenancy. We can guarantee EU-only residency for tenant-scoped production data and backups when requested; implementation details live in the deployment annex. Action: Ben will share the deployment annex snippet with specific language by Jul 29.

- Retention buckets: we can accommodate the split you listed. Action: Kimberly to update the SIG sheet with retention column and control mappings by Jul 28; Jordan will attach SOC2 extracts by Jul 30 (redacted).

- Deletion API: we provide a documented bulk-delete endpoint and an online job that processes within 48-72 hours depending on queue/backfill. Action: Ben to include API SLA language in the DPA response.

I’ve created a Drive folder and added the checklist + a short evidence intake template. HubSpot record is linked below for tracking.

Proposed 30m checkpoint: Jul 30 09:00 PDT — quick walkthrough of SOC2 excerpts and SIG answers. If that works for you, I’ll calendar-inv.

Jordan

On attachments status: I’ll upload SOC2 extract (redacted) and the SIG draft to the Drive by end of day Jul 27.
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Arielle Martin <arielle@finly.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-28 10:17 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & security acceptance sprint — Finly evaluation

Arielle / team — attaching the SIG answers (SIG-answers.xlsx) to the Drive and pasting a short summary here:

- Retention mapping: I added a retention column per control. For EU tenant data we have a region flag and retention enforcement at the object store layer; backups are tagged and retained per the tenant-level policy.
- CAIQ notes: spotlighted controls in the areas of encryption-in-transit, encryption-at-rest (KMS key ownership options), and subprocessor oversight.
- Evidence pointers: control evidence file names live in the Drive folder under /evidence/ (SOC2-extract-stub.pdf, infra-config-snippets.txt, key-rotation-log.csv).

Open item for Finly: can you share a redacted sample of the account-level audit logs you’d like us to validate against? We will run a PII-redaction dry run on a synthetic sample first.

I’ll be on the Jul 30 review.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Security Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Attachments: SIG-answers.xlsx
From: Arielle Martin <arielle@finly.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.g@finly.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-31 15:04 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & security acceptance sprint — Finly evaluation

Jordan / Kimberly — quick note after our 30m review: that was productive and we’re aligned on almost everything. Confirming the outcomes and a short closure path: 

- SOC2 extract received and validated at a high level — Samir will confirm by EOB Jul 31 after internal review.
- SIG answers look complete; Finly security will follow up if we need deeper artifact pulls (Samir asked for the infra-config-snippets.txt).
- DPA redline: we received Ben’s initial response. A small set of language edits remain (retention buckets & deletion SLA wording). Finly legal will send a final redline by Aug 1 morning; Ben to reply within 24 hours.

Subject to the DPA language finishing as discussed, we’re comfortable moving to a final acceptance decision on Aug 2. Thanks for the tight cadence — felt like a clean sprint.

Best,

Arielle
